items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I can't imagine what Irving Mills had to do with that.

ctx.x: Great. So at some point you began playing Ellington -- your band began playing Ellington music. At what point was that?

Oh, that was along around 1937 there. And I got the guys in the band, I said, "Who can I get who can write me some of this stuff?" You know. And so they got me together with a guy by the name of Andy Gibson. And Andy started writing for us, and of course he was very much influenced by the Ellington voicings and the Ellington sound and we got a whole bunch of his arrangements in, and Tizol, you know, was always, he was writing tunes, you know. He'd already done, "Caravan", and "Azure", and he was always giving us…

Well, Irving Mills claims that he took all his raw material and whipped it into shape, and that all of these guys had great ideas and they were just brilliant, but they didn't come up with good names, they didn't write to three minutes, and they didn't know how to make things
